prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your location in Atlanta, budget, system size, brand preference, timeline, and whether you need any ductwork or repairs. I can help you find the best fit; to start, here’s how to pick one and what to ask.

How to choose the best company
- Get at least 3 written estimates so you can compare equipment, scope, and price.
- Prefer contractors that do a Manual J load calculation (not just “rule of thumb”) to right‑size the system.
- Verify license and insurance — ask for their Georgia HVAC license (or business registration) and proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Look for NATE‑certified technicians and manufacturer dealer certifications (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, etc.).
- Check recent reviews on Google, Yelp, and the BBB; ask for local references.
- Confirm they pull permits and follow local code; that protects you and the warranty.
- Compare warranties (equipment vs. labor) and what’s required to keep manufacturer warranty (registration, maintenance schedule).
- Ask about energy‑efficiency options (SEER rating), rebates, and financing.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and present the results?
- What brand/models do you recommend and why? What are the SEER ratings?
- What exactly is included in the install? (new pad, lineset, start kit, thermostat, refrigerant, duct sealing, disposal of old unit)
- Do you provide a written, itemized estimate and timeline?
- What warranties do you offer (parts and labor)? Any transferable warranties?
- Are your technicians NATE certified? Are you a certified dealer for the brand?
- Do you have proof of license and insurance? Will you pull permits?
- Can you provide recent local references or online review links?

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta, rough ballpark)
- Small to mid central A/C replacement (single‑family): roughly $3,500–$8,500 depending on unit capacity and efficiency.
- High‑efficiency or premium brands and extensive ductwork repairs: $8,000–$15,000+.
(Actual price depends on system size, SEER, any ductwork, needed electrical upgrades, and install complexity.)

Brands to consider
- Goodman, Rheem, Ruud — solid value/budget-friendly.
- Trane, Carrier, Lennox — premium, often longer warranties and tighter build quality.
Pick a brand the contractor is certified for and one that matches your budget and efficiency goals.

Next steps I recommend
1. Tell me your Atlanta zip code, budget range, and whether this is a new install or replacement of an existing central AC. I can then help you narrow options and prepare a short message/checklist to send to contractors.
2. Schedule 3 on‑site estimates (avoid giving contractors exact price over the phone).
3. Compare bids based on scope and value, not just lowest price.

If you want, give me your zip code and any other details (house size, existing system, target timeline) and I’ll help you draft outreach messages and a shortlist of what to look for.
